verdict.rationale: Groq's core product is a natural-language chat and Responses API, so users interact with its models in plain language (groq-docs-14, groq-docs-13). A probe also finds an official Groq MCP server (groq-probe-4), and the docs are AI-readable via llms.txt and .md pages (groq-probe-1, groq-probe-2), which would let an agent drive Groq from natural-language requests. However, nothing in the pack describes what that MCP server exposes, or shows account, key, batch or billing management being done through natural-language commands. Missing for 10: documented natural-language control of product operations (keys, batches, spend limits, model selection), details of the MCP server's capabilities, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
